title: Drone Telephoto Beams: Post-Processing, Composition, and Stitching of Saudi 2-2
summary: The video walks through a telephoto drone-shot workflow focused on revealing and enhancing beam-like light structures in a sunrise scene. The presenter opens a 6X RAW frame from a Pro 4 drone, identifies faint beams, and contrasts a quick global adjustment approach with a more deliberate, selective method to bring out beams. Core techniques include expanding dynamic range, dodging to create a directional light source, two-zone RAW edits (foreground vs sky), careful use of dehaze, clarity, and whites to avoid edge halos, and the trade-offs between noise and contrast. The session also covers artistic concepts like the rule of six for composition, color grading iterations, luminosity and history brushes, and a practical workflow for stitching multiple frames—with emphasis on avoiding bracketing and using PTGui when Lightroom isn’t sufficient. The speaker notes practical considerations (gimbal tilt limits, sun/flare, and lens flare) and contrasts easier vs more labor-intensive methods for beam enhancement.
topics: Rule of 20% exposure vs artistic rules
File selection for stitching (RAW vs JPEG)

sections.title: Opening the RAW Telephoto Shot and beam detection
sections.description: The video begins with opening a 6X RAW drone shot, highlighting the Pro 4's 50 MP detail and introducing faint beams present in the frame. This establishes the subject of subsequent tonal and beam-enhancement work.

sections.title: Initial tonal adjustments and directional lighting
sections.description: The presenter uses the dodge tool to simulate a directional light source by lightening mid-tones in key areas and slightly deepening shadows, aligning perceived light direction with the sun. This section emphasizes how light direction affects the eye’s transition and how to plan edits around the sun's location.

sections.title: Two-zone RAW adjustments and edge-halo caution
sections.description: The shot is analyzed as two zones (foreground and sky). The presenter demonstrates using whites, contrast, and clarity while warning that dehaze can introduce edge halos in empty sky regions, guiding the choice toward clarity and controlled adjustments to avoid noise amplification.

sections.title: 60/1000 selective dehaze technique
sections.description: A more advanced method is introduced: applying dehaze selectively with a hard-edge brush using a 60/1000 setup to enhance specific beams, followed by refine-by-eraser with a larger brush to soften one side of the line, creating stronger, more intentional beams.

sections.title: Composition review and one-zone effectiveness; rule of six
sections.description: The speaker discusses cropping, leveling, and avoiding unwanted flat-top artifacts. They emphasize that some drone shots are effectively one-zone images and highlight the rule of six as a compositional check—each sixth of the frame should contribute meaningfully, otherwise it should be removed or re-framed.

sections.title: Beams, sun exposure, and flare considerations
sections.description: A discussion of how beams respond to sun position, how to avoid excessive flare at small apertures, and the interplay between dehaze, color adjustments, and brightness to preserve beam visibility while maintaining overall image integrity.

sections.title: Stitching workflow, bracketing avoidance, and PTGui
sections.description: The speaker emphasizes avoiding bracketing for stitching, selecting suitable frames (non-bracketed RAWs) and managing different folders. They discuss PTGui as a stitching tool, common workflow challenges (e.g., camera updates for newer bodies like Z8), and the general path from RAW exports to stitched panoramas.
